standard_prerequisites.name: Diagonalisation
standard_prerequisites.statement: For any total computable d(x) = Un'(x,x) + 1, d differs from every row Un'(k,.) at x = k.
standard_prerequisites.use: The one-step core of the proof: totality plus computability of Un' would make d total computable and diagonally different from every row.

core_obligations: Statement (lines 1612-1618): any Un'(k,x) universal for the total computable functions (in the stated sense) is not computable.

Diagonal argument (proof lines 1620-1629): if Un' were total and computable, d(x) = Un'(x,x) + 1 would be total computable; but d(k) != Un'(k,k) for every k, so no row of Un' equals d - contradicting universality.
proof_roadmap: Assume Un' total computable and form the diagonal successor d.
Observe d(k) differs from Un'(k,k) by construction.
Conclude no index k realises d, contradicting universality.
difficulty_reason: No universal computable function (statement 1612-1618, proof 1620-1629): a complete diagonalisation in a short span, every step explicit. H2.
